from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # Robot (yellow dot) starting at (1,1) relative to origin D3 -> C4

        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'C2') # One unit left of j-hat tip

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight lecture line
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        # Fade out the initial robot label to keep movement clear
        self.play(FadeOut(robot_label))
        
        # Animate movement: Dot starts at (1,1) [C4]
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid['C6']), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid['B6']), run_time=1.5)
        
        # Final Vector from origin D3 to the robot's end position B6
        final_vector = Arrow(self.grid['D3'], self.grid['B6'], color="#FFFFFF", buff=0, stroke_width=5)
        
        # Replaced MathTex matrix with Text bracket representation to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        vector_coords = Text("[3, 2]", color="#FFFFFF", font_size=28)
        self.place_at_grid(vector_coords, 'A6') # Positioned 1 unit above the vector tip

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        title = "What is a 'Linear' Transformation?"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Transformations move vectors to new positions in space.",
            "The origin must stay fixed in its place.",
            "Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lecture_lines)

        # Define colors as per requirements
        GRID_COLOR = "#444444"
        DOT_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#00FFFF"
        TEXT_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW

        # Create Grid and Origin Dot
        grid_lines = VGroup()
        for i in range(-4, 5):
            grid_lines.add(Line(np.array([i, -4, 0]), np.array([i, 4, 0]), color=GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
            grid_lines.add(Line(np.array([-4, i, 0]), np.array([4, i, 0]), color=GRID_COLOR, stroke_width=1.5))
        
        origin_dot = Dot(point=ORIGIN, color=DOT_COLOR, radius=0.08)
        
        grid_visuals = VGroup(grid_lines, origin_dot)
        self.place_in_area(grid_visuals, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        center_pos = origin_dot.get_center()

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT))
        self.play(Create(grid_lines), FadeIn(origin_dot))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        self.play(
            Rotate(grid_lines, angle=30 * DEGREES, about_point=center_pos),
            grid_lines.animate.scale(1.2, about_point=center_pos),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        self.play(Indicate(origin_dot, color=DOT_COLOR, scale_factor=1.8))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(TEXT_HIGHLIGHT)
        )
        
        self.play(grid_lines.animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        self.wait(1)
        
        grid_lines.save_state()
        
        def wavy_distortion(p):
            rel_p = p - center_pos
            dx = 0.3 * np.sin(rel_p[1] * 1.5)
            dy = 0.3 * np.sin(rel_p[0] * 1.5)
            return center_pos + rel_p + np.array([dx, dy, 0])

        self.play(grid_lines.animate.apply_function(wavy_distortion), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)
        
        self.play(Restore(grid_lines), run_time=2)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        # Setup the title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("The Secret: Tracking the Basis Vectors", [
            "We only need to track i-hat and j-hat.",
            "Their new positions determine the entire transformed grid.",
            "If i-hat moves here and j-hat moves there...",
            "...every other vector follows their lead perfectly.",
            "Tracking basis vectors reveals the secret of space warping."
        ])

        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF7F7F")) # Light Red

            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],

            stroke_width=6

            start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(0, 1),
            buff=0,
            color="#00FF00",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Geometry group
        grid_geom = VGroup(plane, i_hat, j_hat)
        self.place_in_area(grid_geom, 'B2', 'E5')
        
        # Labels for initial basis vectors (Changed from MathTex to Text to avoid missing latex dependency)
        i_label = Text("i", color="#FF0000", font_size=32)
        j_label = Text("j", color="#00FF00", font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(i_label, 'C5')
        self.place_at_grid(j_label, 'B4')
        
        self.play(
            Create(plane), 
            GrowArrow(i_hat), 
            GrowArrow(j_hat), 
            FadeIn(i_label), 
            FadeIn(j_label)
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF7F")) # Light Yellow

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===

            FadeOut(i_label),
            FadeOut(j_label),

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Highlight Line 4
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#7F7FFF")) # Light Blue
        
        # Show an additional vector (1,1) in the new space
        v_orig = Arrow(
            start=plane.coords_to_point(0, 0),
            end=plane.coords_to_point(1, 1),
            buff=0,
            color=WHITE,
            stroke_width=4

        v_label = Text("(1,1)", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(v_label, 'B2')
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(v_orig), FadeIn(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Highlight Line 5
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF7FFF")) # Light Purple

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def create_text_matrix(self, matrix_data, bracket_color=RED):
        """
        Creates a matrix-like mobject using Text instead of MathTex to avoid 
        LaTeX dependencies.
        """
        # Create elements using Text
        elements_group = VGroup(*[
            VGroup(*[Text(str(item), font_size=24) for item in row])
            for row in matrix_data
        ])
        
        # Arrange elements in grid
        for row in elements_group:
            row.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.6)
        elements_group.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.4)
        
        # Create brackets manually using stretched Text objects
        l_brack = Text("[", font_size=48).stretch_to_fit_height(elements_group.height + 0.2)
        l_brack.next_to(elements_group, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        r_brack = Text("]", font_size=48).stretch_to_fit_height(elements_group.height + 0.2)
        r_brack.next_to(elements_group, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        l_brack.set_color(bracket_color)
        r_brack.set_color(bracket_color)
        
        matrix_mob = VGroup(elements_group, l_brack, r_brack)
        
        # Mimic standard Matrix methods
        matrix_mob.get_columns = lambda: VGroup(*[
            VGroup(*[elements_group[r][c] for r in range(len(matrix_data))]) 
            for c in range(len(matrix_data[0]))
        ])
        matrix_mob.get_brackets = lambda: VGroup(l_brack, r_brack)
        
        return matrix_mob

    def construct(self):
        # Initial Setup
        title_text = "Matrices: The Coordinate Containers"
        lecture_lines = [
            "A matrix stores the landing spots of basis vectors.",
            "Column one is i-hat’s new home in space.",
            "Column two is where j-hat lands after transformation.",
            "Matrix multiplication is just a recipe for movement.",
            "It scales or rotates the grid based on coordinates."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Color definitions
        color_1, color_2, color_3, color_4, color_5 = YELLOW, RED, GREEN, BLUE, PURPLE

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(color_1))
        
        # Using custom text-based matrix to avoid LaTeX error
        matrix = self.create_text_matrix([[1, 0], [0, 1]])
        matrix.get_brackets().set_color(RED)
        
        self.place_in_area(matrix, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(color_2))
        col1_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[0], color=color_2, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(col1_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(color_3))
        col2_rect = SurroundingRectangle(matrix.get_columns()[1], color=color_3, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(col2_rect))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(color_4))
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        i_vec = Vector([1, 0], color=color_2)
        j_vec = Vector([0, 1], color=color_3)
        grid_group = VGroup(plane, i_vec, j_vec)
        
        self.place_in_area(grid_group, "D1", "F6", scale_factor=0.4)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_group))
        
        self.play(
            grid_group.animate.apply_matrix([[3, 0], [0, 2]]),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(color_5))
        
        new_matrix = self.create_text_matrix([[3, 0], [0, 2]])
        self.place_in_area(new_matrix, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        label_i = Text("i-hat destination", font_size=14, color=color_2)
        label_j = Text("j-hat destination", font_size=14, color=color_3)
        
        label_i.next_to(new_matrix.get_columns()[0], DOWN, buff=0.2)
        label_j.next_to(new_matrix.get_columns()[1], DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(matrix, new_matrix),
            FadeIn(label_i),
            FadeIn(label_j),
            FadeOut(col1_rect),
            FadeOut(col2_rect)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # Determine the center of the right-side animation area (A1 to F6)
        tl_pos = self.grid["A1"]
        br_pos = self.grid["F6"]
        grid_center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE_D, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        )
        square = Square(side_length=1.5, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        warp_group = VGroup(plane, square)
        self.place_in_area(warp_group, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), Create(square))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # Transformation Sequence: Rotation, Scaling, and Shearing
        angle = 30 * DEGREES
        rot_mat = np.array([
            [np.cos(angle), -np.sin(angle), 0],
            [np.sin(angle),  np.cos(angle), 0],
            [0, 0, 1]
        ])
        
        self.play(
            warp_group.animate.apply_function(
                lambda p: np.dot(rot_mat, p - grid_center) + grid_center
            ),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        scale_mat = np.array([
            [1.3, 0, 0],
            [0, 0.6, 0],
            [0, 0, 1]
        ])
        self.play(
            warp_group.animate.apply_function(
                lambda p: np.dot(scale_mat, p - grid_center) + grid_center
            ),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        shear_mat = np.array([
            [1, 0.7, 0],
            [0, 1, 0],
            [0, 0, 1]
        ])
        self.play(
            warp_group.animate.apply_function(
                lambda p: np.dot(shear_mat, p - grid_center) + grid_center
            ),
            run_time=1.5
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        map_text = Text("Matrices are Geometric Maps", font_size=24, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(map_text, "A3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(map_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        
        # Fix: Manually construct matrix to avoid 'latex' dependency for brackets
        matrix_elements = VGroup(
            Text("a"), Text("b"),
            Text("c"), Text("d")
        ).arrange_in_grid(rows=2, cols=2, buff=0.5)
        
        l_bracket = Text("[", font_size=48).stretch_to_fit_height(matrix_elements.height + 0.2)
        l_bracket.next_to(matrix_elements, LEFT, buff=0.2)
        r_bracket = Text("]", font_size=48).stretch_to_fit_height(matrix_elements.height + 0.2)
        r_bracket.next_to(matrix_elements, RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        final_matrix = VGroup(matrix_elements, l_bracket, r_bracket)
        final_matrix.set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Center the matrix in the right-side area
        self.place_in_area(final_matrix, "A1", "F6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(warp_group),
            FadeOut(map_text),
            FadeIn(final_matrix)
        )
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Linear Transformations and Matrices: The Geometry of Space Warping

sections.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
sections.content: Briefly recap that a vector [x, y] is a movement from the origin. Visualize a 2D coordinate grid with a 'Hero' character (a small robot) standing at (1, 1). Explain that the grid is built on two unit vectors: i-hat (1,0) and j-hat (0,1).
sections.example: If the robot moves 3 steps along i-hat and 2 steps along j-hat, it reaches (3, 2).

sections.title: What is a 'Linear' Transformation?
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a transformation as a 'function' that moves vectors to new positions. For it to be 'Linear', two rules must hold: 1. The origin must remain fixed. 2. Grid lines must remain parallel and evenly spaced after the transformation.
sections.example: Imagine the grid is a rubber sheet. Stretching it or rotating it is linear; bending it into a circle or sliding the center is not.

sections.title: The Secret: Tracking the Basis Vectors
sections.content: Show that to understand where *any* vector goes, we only need to track where i-hat and j-hat land. If we know the new coordinates of i-hat and j-hat, we can deduce the entire transformed grid.
sections.example: If i-hat moves to (0, 1) and j-hat moves to (-1, 0), the entire grid has rotated 90 degrees counter-clockwise.

sections.title: Matrices: The Coordinate Containers
sections.content: Introduce the Matrix as a shorthand way to store these two 'landing' coordinates. The first column is the new i-hat, and the second column is the new j-hat. Multiplying a vector [x, y] by this matrix is just a recipe for where that vector ends up.
sections.example: A matrix [ [3, 0], [0, 2] ] means i-hat is now 3 units long and j-hat is now 2 units tall. This is a 'Scaling' transformation.

sections.title: Application: Transforming 'Yoga Cat'
sections.content: Use a complex shape, like a 2D drawing of a 'Yoga Cat' made of many vectors. Apply a 'Shear' matrix [ [1, 1], [0, 1] ] to show how the cat leans over while its feet stay on the ground.
sections.example: The cat's head at (1, 2) moves to (1*1 + 1*2, 0*1 + 1*2) = (3, 2). The cat appears to be leaning forward to catch a mouse.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Recap that matrices are not just blocks of numbers; they are descriptions of geometric movement. Every matrix multiplication is a transformation of space.
sections.example: A 2x2 matrix is simply a 'map' telling the grid how to dance.

storyboard.title: Prerequisites: Vectors as Directions
lecture_lines: Our robot starts at coordinate one, one.
The grid is built on unit vectors i-hat and j-hat.
Moving two steps along i-hat shifts its horizontal position.
Adding one step along j-hat reaches the target point.
This movement creates the final vector, three comma two.
animations: Create a 2D coordinate grid (#444444) and a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (0,0) that moves to (2,1) leaving a white vector trace.
Highlight a red vector (#FF0000) for i-hat (1,0) and a green vector (#00FF00) for j-hat (0,1).
Animate a yellow dot (#FFFF00) moving 3 units along i-hat, then 2 units along j-hat to reach (3,2).

storyboard.title: What is a 'Linear' Transformation?
lecture_lines: A transformation moves every point on our coordinate grid.
Linear transforms rotate and scale the space evenly.
Notice that grid lines always remain parallel and straight.
Squiggly or curved warping is not a linear transformation.
Critically, the origin must never move from the center.
animations: Show a 2D grid (#444444) with several vectors; all vectors smoothly shift to new locations.
Highlight a white dot (#FFFFFF) at (0,0) that remains stationary while the grid around it rotates.
Change grid line colors to cyan (#00FFFF) and scale the grid uniformly to demonstrate spacing.

storyboard.title: The Secret: Tracking the Basis Vectors
lecture_lines: We only need to track i-hat and j-hat's movements.
Rotating ninety degrees moves them to new landing spots.
These two coordinates fully define how space has warped.
animations: Show the unit vectors i-hat (#FF0000) and j-hat (#00FF00) on a standard grid, making them thicker for emphasis.
Rotate the basis vectors by 45 degrees; the rest of the grid lines follow them precisely.
Move i-hat to (1,1) and j-hat to (-1,1) while keeping them visible as distinct paths.
Animate a blue vector (#0000FF) at (1,0.5) moving to its corresponding transformed position (0.5, 1.5).
Flash the final transformed grid in light grey (#CCCCCC) while keeping basis vectors highlighted.

storyboard.title: Matrices: The Coordinate Containers
lecture_lines: A matrix stores these landing spots in its columns.
Stretching the grid updates the matrix with new values.
Columns represent where basis vectors end up after transformation.
animations: Display an empty 2x2 matrix with red brackets (#FF0000) and placeholders.
Move the current coordinates of the transformed i-hat (3,0) into the first column of the matrix.
Move the current coordinates of the transformed j-hat (0,2) into the second column of the matrix.
Show the matrix [[3,0],[0,2]] next to a vector [1,1] and then show the result [3,2].
Apply the transformation [[3,0],[0,2]] to the entire grid, scaling it 3x horizontally and 2x vertically.

storyboard.title: Application: Transforming 'Yoga Cat'
lecture_lines: Let's apply a shear matrix to our Yoga Cat.
This specific matrix shifts the cat's top horizontally.
Every point on the cat follows the new grid.
A vertex at one, two slides over to three, two.
Matrix math calculates exactly where every point should land.
animations: Create a magenta (#FF00FF) cat-like shape made of connected lines on a grid.
Apply a shear transformation [[1,1],[0,1]] to the cat; the base stays at y=0 while the top shifts right.
Highlight a specific vertex on the cat's ear and show it following a straight horizontal path to its new position.
Briefly show the sheared grid lines in dark blue (#00008B) underneath the cat.
Display the calculation '(1,2) becomes (3,2)' in white text (#FFFFFF) next to the cat's ear vertex.

storyboard.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: Every matrix represents a geometric dance of coordinate space.
Matrices are simple maps for complex spatial transformations.
These numbers describe how we warp and shape reality.
animations: Fade in a 2x2 matrix [[a,b],[c,d]] in gold (#FFD700) and overlay it on a dynamic grid.
Animate the grid quickly cycling through a rotation, then a scale, then a shear.
Fade out all elements except the matrix and the text 'Geometric Maps' in bright green (#00FF00).
